heard: A wealthy businessman spent years hunting for an unseen planet. In 1906, Percival Lowell began searching for Planet X in Arizona. Though Lowell died in 1916, Director V. M. Slipher hired Clyde Tombaugh to continue. Tombaugh discovered Pluto in February 1930 using a new telescope. Decades later, astronomers found Eris in the Kuiper Belt, a body more massive than Pluto. In 2006, the International Astronomical Union required planets to clear their orbital neighborhoods. Pluto failed this criterion and was reclassified as a dwarf planet. NASA's New Horizons later revealed an active world featuring a massive nitrogen ice basin. That ongoing mystery started when a wealthy businessman spent years hunting for an unseen planet.
